summary: Texas, single adult, no children, household earns $55,900/year from work. Based on this, none of the ten programmes look likely. SNAP, WIC, TANF, SSI, EITC, CTC and school meals all have income or household-type requirements this household doesn't meet. Medicaid doesn't cover non-disabled, non-pregnant, childless adults in Texas (no expansion), and the income is well above the limit anyway. CHIP needs children. The ACA premium tax credit is unlikely because the household reports job-based health insurance, which is generally treated as affordable at this income level. Open items: the household was unsure about self-employment, which would not change the result at this income. If the employer plan is unaffordable or the person loses job coverage, the ACA premium tax credit should be rechecked through the Marketplace.
